risk_if_not_implemented: Without Redundant Secondary System, data, software and system images cannot be reliably restored within required recovery objectives following a disruption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Data Loss / Integrity Compromise (R-BC-2), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Data Backup & Restoration Hardware Protection
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to protect data backup and restoration hardware and software.
compensating_control_1.justification: Data Backup & Restoration Hardware Protection (BCD-31) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Redundant Secondary System (BCD-21) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Backups
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Backups (BCD-24) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Redundant Secondary System (BCD-21) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
